title: Product PRD & Release Overview: Unified Inference - Roadmap, Pricing, and Q4 Release Notes
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap themes for the Unified Inference initiative, pricing and packaging guidance, and the release notes for the Q4 2026 release (release date: 2026-12-20). It is intended for product, engineering, GTM, and partner stakeholders.

Goals (what success looks like)

- Provide a single product surface that unifies hosted, dedicated, and private deployment flows under the Unified Inference brand.
- Deliver predictable unit economics: improve cost per 1k tokens by 18% for typical RLHF chat workloads via batching, quantization profiles, and routing.
- Make enterprise adoption frictionless: provide pricing/packaging options and a documented migration path.
- Maintain production SLOs: 95th percentile request latency < 250ms for short-form generation (<= 128 tokens) and 99.95% availability for Dedicated customers.

Product overview (short)

Unified Inference: a converged product offering that exposes a single API and console experience for: hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private. Key surfaces included in this release: model routing policies, quantization profile marketplace, per-route cost controls, and an admin migration guide for Private deployments.

Key use cases and personas

- ML Engineers: model selection, benchmarking, and quantization guidance for production serving.
- Platform Engineers: rollout configuration, autoscaling rules, and observability dashboards.
- Product teams: cost-aware generation settings and per-route quality guardrails.
- Enterprise customers: private deployment packaging and audit-ready compliance artifacts.

PRD summary & prioritized requirements

1) Core API parity (MUST)
   - Same REST/SDK surface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (endpoints, streaming, function/tool calling).
   - Backwards-compatible request schema; opt-in to new fields via version header.

2) Model routing and fallbacks (MUST)
   - Policy engine that routes by latency, cost, region, and customer tier.
   - Automatic fallback to compatible model variants when primary capacity unavailable.
   - Admin UI for route policies + audit logging.

3) Quantization profiles and recommendations (MUST)
   - Profile catalog with recommended quantization settings per model-family/workload.
   - Compatibility matrix indicating accuracy delta (validation set) and throughput improvements.

4) Cost & performance controls (MUST)
   - Per-route batching configuration with default safe presets.
   - Token-level cost estimation in Console and API response headers.

5) Pricing & packaging (SHOULD)
   - New tiered packages: Developer (pay-as-you-go), Standard (committed monthly), Enterprise (reserved Dedicated + support).
   - Add-ons: extended observability retention, SOC2-compliant evidence package, private deployment licensing.

6) Migration & on-prem path (SHOULD)
   - Clear migration playbook for Dedicated -> Private, including network prerequisites, KMS setup, and data residency checklist.

7) Telemetry & quality monitoring (SHOULD)
   - Per-prompt/eval hooks to detect regressions; integrate with Redwood Optimize quality alerts.

Non-functional requirements

- Latency: p95 < 250ms for <=128 tokens; p99 < 1.2s for <=512 tokens for Hosted by default.
- Availability: Hosted target 99.9% global; Dedicated SLA 99.95%.
- Throughput: system should sustain 4x baseline traffic for canary rollouts without manual intervention.
- Security/compliance: all Private releases must support customer-managed KMS and audit logging.

Design notes and architecture (high level)

- Policy Engine: implemented as a control-plane service (policy-store + evaluator). Policies are versioned and stored in the Config DB. Runtime agents load policies and report decisions to tracing.
- Quantization Catalog: a metadata service that stores profile artifacts (profile id, model-family, quantization level, expected throughput uplift, expected accuracy delta). Profiles are immutable once published; the Console supports staged rollout of a profile to a percentage of traffic.
- Routing and Fallbacks: requests flow through the Router service which consults policy and KV cache. If selected capacity is unavailable, Router triggers a fallback path that includes model-variant substitution and dynamic batching adjustments.
- Observability: per-route dashboards (latency, tokens, cost), integrated tracing and error budgets exposed to the Console.

Design constraints and decisions

- We prioritize backward compatibility for API consumers; new features are opt-in via headers or route config.
- Quantization profiles are advisory by default; operators must enable enforced quantization per route.
- Fallbacks avoid downgrading to models with known quality regressions on guardrail prompts.

Roadmap & themes (Q3 2026 - Q2 2027)

- Q3 2026: Policy engine MVP, basic quantization catalog, per-route batching controls, beta pricing tiers.
- Q4 2026: Console integration (policy editor), profile marketplace, private deployment migration playbook, release notes and GTM materials (this release).
- Q1 2027: Autoscaling improvements for Dedicated, advanced rollouts (A/B + canary based on quality signals), extended eval integration.
- Q2 2027: Multi-region private deployments, HSM integrations for KMS, expanded enterprise packaging and compliance bundles.

Pricing & packaging guidance (summary)

Tiers (high-level):
- Developer (PAYG): $0.002 per 1k tokens generation baseline, $0.00075 per 1k tokens embeddings; 100k free tokens monthly trial for new signups. No SLA.
- Standard (Committed): Volume discounts tied to monthly committed usage (example: 10% off at $10k/mo, 20% off at $50k/mo). Includes basic console features and 30-day observability retention.
- Enterprise (Reserved Dedicated / Private): Custom pricing (typically annual commitments). SLA: 99.95% availability for Dedicated. Includes onboarding support, extended observability retention (1 year), and SOC2 evidence.
- Add-ons: Private deployment license ($Xk one-time + monthly support), extended retention, model-eval credits, on-site migration assistance.

Note: Pricing numbers above are illustrative for GTM planning. Final list prices approved by Finance and Legal must be captured in the pricing catalog and updated in the Billing service prior to public announcement.

Packaging decisions for sales enablement

- Bundle commonly paired items (e.g., Dedicated + 6 months onboarding + 1 year observability) into named SKUs for simpler quoting.
- Provide migration credits for existing Dedicated customers who move to Private within the first 6 months post-release.

Release notes - 2026-12-20 (Q4 release)

Highlights
- Policy engine v1 & Console policy editor: create and version routing policies, target by latency/cost/region.
- Quantization profile marketplace v1: publish, stage, and roll out profiles; surfaced throughput/accuracy estimates.
- Per-route cost controls and token-level cost estimates in Console and API response headers.
- Migration playbook for Dedicated -> Private, including network, KMS, and packaging checklist.

Breaking changes
- None for standard API consumers. New features require opt-in.

Known issues / limitations
- Profile validation for some large model families (>= 70B) is staged; we recommend manual verification before full rollout.
- Console policy editor currently supports JSON/YAML import only; richer UI helpers will be added in Q1 2027.

Rollout plan and schedule

1) Internal canary (2026-12-21 to 2026-12-23)
   - Target: 5% internal traffic; engineering + solutions teams.
   - Acceptance criteria: no SLO regressions, automated smoke tests green, no critical errors in logs.

2) Hosted beta (2026-12-24 to 2027-01-07)
   - Target: selected customers and early adopters.
   - Monitoring: per-route dashboards, cost telemetry, and quality guardrail evaluations.

3) General availability (2027-01-10)
   - GA gating: completed migrations for pilot customers, no critical regressions, finance approval for public pricing.

- Policy editor import/export tests - pass.

- Private migration dry-run with 1 pilot customer - completed.

Appendix: sample policy JSON (example, opt-in)

{
  "policy_id": "policy-unified-2026-12",
  "priority": 10,
  "rules": [
    {
      "match": { "region": "eu", "customer_tier": "enterprise" },
      "action": { "route_to": "dedicated-eu-1" }
    },
    {
      "match": { "latency_budget_ms": 200 },
      "action": { "prefer": ["model-a-quantized", "model-a"] }
    }
  ]
}

(Consumers should treat this as example; policies are versioned in Config DB.)
